records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
As an F-1 or J-1 graduate student, you need to be registered for **at least 9 credits** each term to be full-time ([ISSS: Maintaining Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)).

Key conditions:
- **Online courses:** No more than 3 credits of online/distance coursework can count toward full-time enrollment. That means at least 6 of your 9 credits must be face-to-face or hybrid.
- **Audited courses** don't count toward the full-time minimum ([ISSS: Less Than Full Time](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time)).
- **Dropping below 9 credits:** You need written permission from ISSS before the term begins to enroll less than full-time. Don't drop or withdraw from a course mid-semester without approval from an ISSS advisor. Students who fall below full-time without authorization are considered out of immigration status.

If you think you may need a reduced course load, contact an ISSS advisor before making any changes.

records.question: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?

records.answer:
No more than 3 credits of online or distance coursework can count toward your full-time enrollment each term. So undergraduates need at least 9 credits, and graduate students at least 6 credits, that meet face-to-face or in a hybrid format ([ISSS: Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)).

If you're unsure how a specific course is classified, or you need to go below full-time, check with an ISSS advisor first. Don't drop or withdraw from a course without ISSS approval.

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
records.answer:
F-1 and J-1 students can work **up to 20 hours per week** on campus while school is in session ([On-Campus Employment](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/on-campus-employment)). During an approved vacation term, immigration regulations allow more than 20 hours, but you need to check the Office of Human Resources for their own policies on that.

Some key conditions:
- You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, be a continuing student, not have graduated, and have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019 ([Maintaining Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)).
- J-1 students must get ISSS authorization before starting any on-campus job.
- If you're on co-op, your co-op counts as your "class," so on-campus work is still limited to 20 hours per week. ISSS strongly discourages doing both at the same time.
- On-campus work shouldn't affect your academic performance.

If your curriculum requires you to work more than 20 hours per week on campus, you must apply for CPT ([CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)).

For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
F-1 students have a **60-day grace period** after their program ends, and F-1 dependents get the same 60 days ([ISSS: Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)). The same 60 days applies after post-completion OPT ends, but only if you completed the OPT and did not exceed the 90-day unemployment limit ([ISSS: OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.

You may **not** work or study.

**What's expected:** If you are not applying for OPT or extending your legal status, you should leave the U.S. within the grace period. If you leave before it ends, you can't re-enter on your F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date.

**If you apply for OPT:** If USCIS receives your application before the 60 days end, your F-1 status stays active until USCIS decides, and you can remain in the U.S. while it's pending ([ISSS: OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).

**Possible future change:** In September 2025, DHS proposed ending "duration of status" and cutting the F-1 grace period from 60 to 30 days. This is only a proposed rule, and the excerpts I have don't show that it has been finalized ([ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/September/DHS-Proposes-to-Replace-Duration-of-Status-for-F-and-J-Visa-Holders-with-Fixed-Periods-of-Stay)). For your specific situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How much OPT can I get?
search_queries: How much OPT can I get?
records.answer:
You can get **12 months of standard OPT for each degree level** (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use part of it during your program (Pre-Completion OPT) or save all 12 months for after graduation (Post-Completion OPT). Pre-completion OPT counts against your 12 months differently depending on the schedule: full-time counts at 100%, and part-time counts at 50%. For example, 6 months of part-time pre-completion OPT uses 3 months. ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt))

**STEM OPT Extension:** If you're in a STEM field and meet the criteria, you may be eligible for an additional 24 months of Post-Completion OPT. You can't request all 36 months at once. You must first apply for the initial 12 months of Post-Completion OPT, then apply for the extension while your OPT EAD card is active. ([STEM OPT Extension page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension))

**Proposed fee rule:** On October 7, DHS proposed a rule that would require universities to pay a $70,000 fee for each OPT and $30,000 for STEM OPT requests. ISSS says this has no immediate impact, and current OPT and STEM OPT processes remain unchanged unless DHS finalizes and implements the rule. ([ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT))

For your specific situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
You can be unemployed for a maximum of **90 days** in total while on Post-Completion OPT. [ISSS explains](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) that this is an aggregate limit, so all your unemployment days add up across the whole OPT period.

Key details:
- Every day counts, including weekends, from the employment start date shown on your EAD when you don't have qualifying employment.
- Exceeding the limit is a violation of F-1 status. Your SEVIS record may be terminated, and students who exceed it aren't eligible for the 60-day grace period.
- Before you reach the limit, you should prepare to transfer to another SEVP-certified school, change educational level, depart the U.S., or otherwise act to maintain status.
- Qualifying work on Post-Completion OPT must be at least 20 hours per week.

If you later get a 24-month STEM OPT extension, you get an [additional 60 days](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension), for a maximum of 150 days total. You must report any interruption or loss of employment to ISSS.

For your own situation, such as how many days you've already accrued, please confirm with your ISSS advisor.

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
search_queries: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
records.answer:
No, you don't need a job offer to apply for OPT. [ISSS states](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) that a job offer is not required for either Pre-Completion or Post-Completion OPT.

Some conditions apply once you're on OPT:

- **Post-Completion OPT:** You're expected to actively seek work in your field of study and be employed for at least nine months after your OPT start date (as shown on your EAD). You can accrue a maximum of 90 days of unemployment in total. Each day, including weekends, without qualifying employment counts toward that limit. Before you reach the limit, you should prepare to transfer, change educational level, depart the U.S., or take another action to maintain status.
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** There's no penalty for not working, but that time is deducted from your 12 months of OPT eligibility.
- **You can't start working early:** Don't begin work before you have your EAD card and before the start date printed on it.

A job offer is different for the 24-month STEM OPT extension. [That extension requires](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) a job or job offer directly related to your STEM degree, from an E-Verify employer.

For advice on your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
No. Self-employment doesn't qualify for the 24-month STEM OPT extension. The [STEM OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) says the regulations require a bona fide employer-employee relationship with an employer.

- You can work for a start-up, but all regulatory requirements must still be met. You may not provide the employer attestations on your own behalf.
- Your STEM OPT employer must also have an EIN, use E-Verify at your worksite, and offer a job directly related to your STEM degree.

Self-employment is treated differently during standard Post-Completion OPT. [The OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) says you may start a business then, but you must work full-time and be able to prove you have the proper business licenses and are actively engaged in a business related to your degree. That allowance doesn't carry over to the STEM extension.

If you're planning to run your own company, please confirm your options with an ISSS advisor before making decisions about your status.

records.question: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
search_queries: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
records.answer:
Yes. Your STEM OPT employer must be enrolled in E-Verify and using it at your STEM OPT worksite. - Your employer also needs an Employment Identification Number (EIN), and the job must be directly related to your qualifying STEM degree.

If you don't know it, ask your supervisor or the company's HR department.
- If you work for more than one employer, each must meet all the requirements, including E-Verify.
- If you change employers during STEM OPT, the new employer must also be enrolled in E-Verify. You must report the change to ISSS within 10 days using the [STEM OPT Employment Update Form](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-opt-employment.pdf).

If you're unsure whether your employer qualifies, contact ISSS at ISSS@drexel.edu or 215.895.2502.

records.question: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
search_queries: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
records.answer:
The answer depends on your F-1 situation:

- **Most F-1 students:** The [Travel Information page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel) says your I-20 needs a travel signature issued within **12 months** of re-entry.
- **F-1 students on Post-Completion OPT or STEM OPT:** The signature may not be older than **6 months**. The [OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) and the [STEM OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) both say this.

**A discrepancy to be aware of:** The [Visa Renewal page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/visa-renewal) says to request a new signature if yours will be more than six months old when you return. The 2024 [re-entry advisory](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2024/December/re-entry) only asks for a "recent" signature. Because the pages differ, the safe choice is to have a signature no more than 6 months old on your return date. You can confirm with an ISSS advisor.

If you need a new signature, submit the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs) before you travel.

records.question: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?
search_queries: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?
records.answer:
The amount depends on your visa type. In both cases, it's in addition to the funds covering your own tuition, fees, and living expenses.

**F-1 students (I-20):** You need to show **$4,000 for a spouse plus $2,000 for one child, so $6,000 total**. This applies [regardless of how long your dependents will stay in the U.S.](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/dependents)

**J-1 students (DS-2019):** The J-2 requirement is stated per month: [$600/month for a spouse and $400/month for each child](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars). For a spouse and one child, that is $1,000/month. The excerpts don't say how many months you must show, so please confirm the total with ISSS.

Note that the J-1 page is aimed at J-1 scholars, while the dependents page covers both F-1 and J-1 students. The dependents page lists only the F-1-style amounts ($4,000 and $2,000), so if you are a J-1 student, it's worth asking an ISSS advisor which figure applies to you.

**To apply:** Submit the Add a Dependent form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx) with:
- A copy of each dependent's passport
- An updated official bank statement
- Proof of marriage
- Proof of birth for your child

records.question: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
search_queries: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
records.answer:
Yes, possibly. F-1 and J-1 students in their final term can apply for less than full time (LTFT) under "Completion of Studies" if the credits they still need to finish their degree are fewer than full-time enrollment requires. [ISSS's LTFT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time) lists these conditions:

- **Online limits:** You can't take courses fully online in your final term. If you need more than one class, no more than one class (3 credits) of online study can count toward your remaining requirements.
- **Medical LTFT:** Students in their final term who are approved for medical LTFT must enroll in at least one course.

**How to apply:**
1. Complete the Less Than Full-Time form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx). Your academic advisor must specify the reason and sign it.
2. Email it to isss@drexel.edu before you drop below full time.
3. Wait for ISSS's approval email before dropping any credits.

Requests are due by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term). Dropping below full time without ISSS authorization puts you out of status. ISSS also advises that you [shouldn't drop or withdraw from a course](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain) without first getting approval from an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How do I apply for CPT?
search_queries: How do I apply for CPT?
records.answer:
To apply for CPT, first confirm that the training is a required part of your program, then submit your application to ISSS.

**Before applying, check that you:**
- Have been enrolled full-time and physically present in the U.S. for at least one full academic year (3 quarters or 2 semesters). There is an exception for graduate students whose programs require immediate CPT.
- Have an internship or training offer directly related to your field.
- Are in a program where the practical training is required for all students to graduate. If there's an associated course, you must be registered for it during the CPT term.

**Steps** ([CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)):
1. **Co-op students:** meet with your Steinbright Career Development Center Co-op Advisor to start the process.
2. **Non-co-op students:** meet with your academic advisor to confirm the CPT is required by your program's curriculum.

records.question: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?

1. **Get a medical letter.** It must be on official letterhead and signed by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist. Your doctor doesn't need to give diagnosis details but should use the template on the page, and the letter must include everything the template requires. - Submit by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).
- Approval is needed for each term you request.
- Medical LTFT is limited to 12 aggregate months per program level.
- You're expected to return to full-time study afterward.

- Send your documents to ISSS at least 30 days before your OPT EAD end date.
- USCIS must receive your application within 60 days of the date ISSS prints your I-20.

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
**CPT** and **OPT** are both F-1 work authorizations, but they differ in purpose, who approves them, and when you can use them.

**CPT (Curricular Practical Training)**
- It is off-campus work authorization for an internship, co-op, practicum, or other training that is a **required part of your academic program's curriculum**. It is driven by curriculum requirements, not by your wish to work. Work that is merely beneficial or good experience doesn't qualify ([CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)).
- **ISSS** reviews and authorizes it ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).
- Dates follow the official term dates in the Drexel academic calendar, and you can't start work before the CPT start date. Most CPT is authorized term by term, while Steinbright-designated co-ops follow the co-op cycle dates.

**OPT (Optional Practical Training)**
- It is temporary employment directly related to your major and appropriate to your degree level. It is available before you finish your studies (Pre-Completion) and after (Post-Completion) ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).
- You apply to **USCIS**, which can take 90 days or longer.
- A job offer isn't required to apply.
- Eligibility requires one full academic year of full-time enrollment and lawful F-1 status.

**How they connect:** Using 364 days or more of full-time CPT eliminates your OPT eligibility. Part-time CPT and international co-op don't affect it ([CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)).

To decide which fits your situation, I'd recommend talking with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: I graduated and my OPT is approved. What do I need to travel abroad and come back?

records.question: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
search_queries: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
records.answer:
It depends on the type and amount of CPT.

- **Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates your eligibility for OPT.** The [OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) says you must have fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT at your current educational level. Accumulating more than 364 days of full-time CPT is also listed as a common reason OPT applications are denied.
- **Part-time CPT or international co-op does not affect OPT eligibility**, according to the [CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt).

Because the limit is tied to full-time CPT, check how many days of full-time CPT you've accumulated before you take on more. An ISSS advisor can confirm where you stand and how your specific plan would count.

**About the duration-of-status rule:** The CPT page mentions a DHS final rule that was scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. A [newer ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) (September 14, 2026) says a federal court postponed it, so it did not go into effect on that date. records.question: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
search_queries: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
records.answer:
Yes, but it's strongly discouraged. F-1 and J-1 students may work on campus during a co-op cycle, but [ISSS says](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/on-campus-employment) doing both at the same time is not recommended.

Key conditions:
- **20-hour limit:** While you're on co-op, your co-op job counts as your "class," so on-campus work is limited to 20 hours per week.
- **Co-op comes first:** On-campus work must not interfere with your responsibilities at your co-op job.
- **Valid status:** You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, and your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired.
- **J-1 students:** You must get permission from ISSS before starting any on-campus job. Email isss@drexel.edu with your job offer (position title and expected start and end dates) before accepting.
- **F-1 students:** You don't need advance ISSS approval, but you'll need your documents ready for onboarding and the I-9 with Drexel HR.

If your co-op is in the U.S. and off campus, it generally needs separate work authorization, and I couldn't find the details of that in the excerpts I have. Please confirm your specific situation with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
search_queries: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?

- Có lời mời thực tập/đào tạo liên quan trực tiếp đến ngành học.

- CPT không được làm chậm thời gian tốt nghiệp.

Bạn cần trao đổi với cố vấn của mình (cố vấn Co-op của Steinbright nếu học chương trình co-op, hoặc cố vấn học tập nếu không) rồi nộp đơn CPT cho ISSS qua [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

records.question: OPT申请需要多长时间？

records.question: ¿Cuántas horas por semana puedo trabajar en el campus?

records.question: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
search_queries: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
records.answer:
F-1 학생(및 동반 가족)의 졸업 후 유예 기간은 **60일**입니다. J-1 학생은 30일입니다. [ISSS 안내 페이지](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)에 따르면, 유예 기간에는 다음이 가능합니다.

- 짐을 싸고 출국을 준비하는 것
- 미국 내 여행

이 기간에는 일하거나 공부할 수 **없습니다**. OPT를 신청하지 않거나 체류 자격 연장을 받지 않는 학생은 유예 기간 안에 출국해야 합니다. 유예 기간이 끝나기 전에 출국하면 I-20/DS-2019 만료일 이후에는 F-1/J-1 신분으로 재입국할 수 없습니다.

**OPT/STEM OPT의 경우:** OPT EAD 카드가 만료된 뒤에도 60일의 유예 기간이 있습니다. 다만 OPT 기간을 모두 마친 학생에게만 적용되며, 실업 한도(OPT 90일, STEM OPT 150일)를 초과한 학생은 유예 기간을 받을 수 없습니다. 자세한 내용은 [OPT 페이지](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)와 [STEM OPT 페이지](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)에서 확인하세요.

**규정 변경 가능성:** 2025년 9월에 발표된 [DHS 제안 규칙](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/September/DHS-Proposes-to-Replace-Duration-of-Status-for-F-and-J-Visa-Holders-with-Fixed-Periods-of-Stay)은 F-1 유예 기간을 30일로 줄이는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 한편 ISSS 홈페이지에 따르면 2026년 9월 14일 미국 연방지방법원이 체류 기간(D/S) 폐지 최종 규칙의 시행을 연기하는 가처분 명령을 내렸습니다. 이 점에 대해 제가 가진 자료로는 자세한 내용을 확인할 수 없으니, 본인의 상황은 ISSS 상담원에게 확인하시기 바랍니다.

records.question: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
search_queries: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
records.answer:
Sim. Para F-1, o ISSS lista como documento obrigatório de reentrada um I-20 válido com **assinatura de viagem emitida nos últimos 12 meses** antes da reentrada (ou 6 meses, se você estiver em OPT pós-conclusão/STEM). Veja a [página de viagens](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel). Para STEM OPT, a assinatura não pode ter mais de 6 meses, conforme a [página de STEM OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension).

records.question: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
search_queries: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
records.answer:
It depends on how long you're away.

**You must pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again** if you haven't been enrolled for more than five (5) months, or if your SEVIS record was terminated for a reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal." In those cases you need a new I-20/DS-2019 and must [repay the SEVIS I-901 fee](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/vacation-loa). Email ISSS at least three (3) months before your planned return to get instructions on applying for the new I-20/DS-2019.

**You don't need a new I-20 or fee** in the case of an ISSS-authorized absence of less than five months. There, you can request a SEVIS record reactivation by submitting these 1-2 months before you return:
- I-94 travel history showing your departure
- A flight itinerary with your planned re-entry date
- Proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term

SEVP has discretion over reactivation. If it isn't approved, you'd need a new I-20 instead.

Also, a new I-20 means a break in F-1 status. You must complete at least one academic year of full-time study before becoming eligible for benefits like CPT or OPT.

You'll also need approval from your academic program to return from leave. For your specific situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

To pay the fee, ISSS points to [FMJfee.com](https://fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html) (external site).

records.question: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
search_queries: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
records.answer:
The two-year home-country physical presence requirement (212(e)) means certain J-1 exchange visitors can't become lawful permanent residents or change to another visa status in the U.S. until they've lived and been physically present in their country of nationality or last legal permanent residence for at least two years after leaving the U.S. in J-1 status.

**Who it applies to** ([J-1 page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars)):
- Those whose program was financed, in whole or part, directly or indirectly, by a U.S. government agency or by the government of their home country.
- Those from a country that the U.S. Department of State has designated as needing people with the specialized skill or knowledge they pursued (the "skills list").

For students, ISSS says that government funding or a major on the home country's skills list can make you subject to it ([New International Students page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/new-international-students)).

**Waiver:**
- You may be able to apply for a waiver, but ISSS may not assist with J-1 waivers because the Department of State considers that a conflict of interest for program sponsors. Instead, see the [Department of State's waiver guidance](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html) (external).
- Waiver cases can take a year or longer, and applying for or receiving one doesn't automatically extend your legal stay.
- After a favorable recommendation, you're no longer eligible for J-1 extension, transfer, or a new J-1 visa.

**H-1B impact:** If you're subject to 212(e), you can't begin H-1B employment until you've received a waiver ([H-1B FAQ](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/h1b-temp/h1b-faq)).

records.question: H-1B cap-gap extension
search_queries: H-1B cap-gap extension
records.answer:
**H-1B cap-gap** is the period between the end of your OPT (or STEM OPT) and the start of your H-1B status. If you have a timely filed change of status to H-1B, your work authorization is automatically extended while it's pending.

**Eligibility** ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)):
- Your employer files the H-1B petition on or after April 1 and requests a change of status.
- You are still within your OPT authorization period when it is filed.

**Length of the extension:** ISSS's OPT and STEM OPT pages describe the extension as running through October 1 or until the change of status is approved. However, a [January 16, 2025 ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/January/USCIS-DHS-Announces-H-1B-Modernization-Rule) says the H-1B Modernization Rule extends the cap-gap period to as late as April 1 of the following year. Because the pages differ, please confirm with ISSS which applies to you.

**To get a cap-gap I-20** ([STEM OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)):
1. Email ISSS to make sure your employment and address information is correct. Wrong information in SEVIS significantly delays the I-20.
2. Email ISSS one of the following:
   - For an extension through June 1: an employer statement that the H-1B change of status was properly filed, plus proof of delivery to USCIS.
   - For an extension beyond June 1: a scanned USCIS receipt or proof the petition was wait-listed.

ISSS will email you when your new I-20 is ready.

**Good to know:**
- If the petition is denied, rejected, or revoked, work permission ends on your EAD end date (if still valid) or on the date of the denial, rejection, revocation, or withdrawal.
- The unemployment limit continues during cap-gap.
- Check with your employer or immigration attorney before traveling abroad.

For questions about your own situation, please contact an ISSS advisor.

You can file for the STEM OPT extension up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date. So the practical window is from 90 days before your EAD expires to about 30 days before, with the 30-day mark being the latest to submit to ISSS. Earlier within that window gives you more buffer.

If you receive an RFE or your application is returned or rejected, contact ISSS immediately.

**Trong 12 tháng OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp, bạn được tối đa 90 ngày thất nghiệp (tính gộp).** Nếu bạn sau đó được duyệt gia hạn STEM OPT 24 tháng, bạn được thêm 60 ngày, tổng tối đa là 150 ngày ([trang STEM OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)).

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày, kể cả cuối tuần, mà bạn không có việc làm đủ điều kiện kể từ ngày bắt đầu OPT ghi trên thẻ EAD đều tính là một ngày thất nghiệp ([trang OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).

**Nếu sắp hết giới hạn:**
- Trước ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng, bạn phải thực hiện một trong các việc sau: chuyển sang trường SEVP khác hoặc đổi bậc học, rời khỏi Hoa Kỳ, hoặc có hành động khác để duy trì tình trạng hợp pháp. Nếu không, bạn vi phạm tình trạng di trú.
- Sinh viên vượt quá 90 ngày thất nghiệp không được hưởng thời gian ân hạn 60 ngày.

**Báo cáo:** Bạn phải báo cho ISSS nếu bị gián đoạn hoặc mất việc. Trong thời gian STEM OPT, bạn còn phải nộp bản đánh giá cuối cùng trên Form I-983 trong vòng 10 ngày nếu mất việc hoặc nghỉ việc.

Để biết số ngày thất nghiệp còn lại của riêng bạn hoặc cách xử lý tình huống cụ thể, hãy liên hệ cố vấn ISSS.
